userStories.title: Model, reducer and engine-native core metrics
userStories.description: As a user without `cctop install`, I want context, cost, rate limits and the current turn tracked live from the engine, so that the pane is useful with zero setup.
acceptanceCriteria: `plugin/hooks/model.ts` exports the `Model` type (`usage: SessionUsage | null`, `usageAt`, `turn: { number, state: 'idle'|'busy'|'waiting', startedAt, lastDurationMs, lastReason, runningTool: { name, startedAt } | null }`, `tools: Record<name, { calls, errors, durationsMs: number[], tokensToCtx }>`, `compactions`, `binary: 'unknown'|'present'|'missing'`, `view`, `open`, `stale`, `placement`) and `initialModel()`

`plugin/hooks/model.ts` exports a pure `reduce(model, action) => Model` where actions are `session.start`, `turn.start`, `turn.complete` (`durationMs`, `reason`), `tool.start` (name, at), `tool.end` (name, at, isError, resultChars), `session.compact`, `usage` (a `SessionUsage` + at); no `$` inside

`plugin/hooks/pane.tsx` registers hooks for `session.start`, `turn.start`, `turn.complete`, `session.compact`, and `tool.call` wrapping `next(e)`: it records the start timestamp, calls `next(e)`, then records the end with `isError` and `text.length` from the result; the hook's own work before `next(e)` is timestamps/counters only

`$.session.usage()` is read only from a `$.clock.every(1000)` timer that runs while `turn.state === 'busy'` and once after `turn.complete` and `session.start`; it is never awaited before `next(e)` in any hook
Every registration has `.catch(err => $.ui.log(...))`; every hook returns what `next(e)` returned, unchanged

Tests (`tests/pane/reducer.test.ts`): a scripted sequence start -> tool.call x3 (one `isError: true`, result texts of 400/4000/40 chars) -> compact -> complete yields calls 3, errors 1, p50 of the durations, `tokensToCtx` = ceil(chars/4) summed, `lastReason`, compactions 1; a usage action from `fixtures/usage.json` produces formatted rows `tokens / window (percent %)`, `five_hour`/`seven_day` `percentUsed` with a countdown from a fixed `now` to `resetsAt`, and `cost.usd` with two decimals
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: `tool.end` carries `startedAt` besides name/at/isError/resultChars (the hook keeps it in its closure) so concurrent calls of one tool time themselves apart and only the matching call clears `runningTool`. `turn.state` `waiting` is declared but never set yet (permission waits need `tool.check`, PRD open question 4). Model state and the `$`-taking helpers (`apply`, `readUsage`, `startUsageTimer`) live at module scope: `claude plugin validate --strict` refuses `$` passed to a closure. The render draws an interim turn/running-tool/usage list until US-005 replaces it with the Overview.

userStories.title: Binary detection and query poller
userStories.description: As a user with the `cctop` binary installed, I want the pane to pull deep metrics from `cctop query`, so that it matches the TUI.
acceptanceCriteria: On load (`session.start`), `$.process.run(["cctop", "--version"], { timeoutMs: 3000 })` sets `model.binary` to `present` (exit 0) or `missing` (rejects or non-zero); `missing` is shown as one header line `needs the cctop binary: brew install tomstagl/tap/cctop` and disables the poller

`plugin/hooks/poller.ts` exports `createPoller($, getModel, setModel)` with `start()`, `stop()`, `tick()`: each tick runs `cctop query <verb> --session <id>` for verbs `summary`, `tools`, `files`, `agents`, `advice`, `events` sequentially through ONE in-flight promise (a tick that starts while one runs is skipped), each with `timeoutMs: 5000`; the JSON is parsed into `model.query[verb]`
Cadence: 2000 ms while `turn.state === 'busy'`, 10000 ms otherwise, re-evaluated after every `turn.start`/`turn.complete`
A failed or non-JSON call keeps the previous `model.query[verb]`; `model.stale` becomes true when the last successful tick is older than 30 s
The verbs the binary supports are read once from `cctop query --help`; a verb absent there is never called and its section reads `unsupported by this cctop version`
Precedence documented in code: Context and Limits rows come from `model.usage` when present, else from `query.summary`; everything else from the query JSON
Every tick refreshes the marker file `~/.cctop/pane/<sessionId>.json` (see US-008) — stub the write here as `writeMarker($, model)` so US-008 only fills in the shape

Tests (`tests/pane/poller.test.ts`) with the scripted `process.run` and manual clock: busy cadence 2 s, idle 10 s; a slow (never-resolving) `summary` blocks further ticks without overlap; stale after 30 s of failures; `binary: missing` spawns no `query`; an unsupported verb is skipped
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: `claude plugin validate --strict` follows `$` only into functions declared in the same file, never across an import, so `createPoller` cannot take `$` itself: it takes `PollerEngine` (the slice of `$` it uses: clock.now/every, process.run, session.id, fs.write, ui.log, plus `home()` for `$.env.get("HOME")`, whose name the validator reads off pane.tsx), built by the top-level `pollerEngine($)` in pane.tsx; the fake `$` is structurally assignable, so tests call `createPoller({ ...$, home }, getModel, setModel)`. The poller runs while the pane is open and the binary is present (US-008 adds the stop on ui.close); `reschedule()` re-arms the cadence after turn.start/turn.complete and is a no-op while stopped. A tick is successful when every called verb parsed; `stale` is judged in the timer callback before each tick, so a hung query flips it too. A failed `--help` leaves `verbs` null (every verb tried, help retried next tick). `writeMarker` already writes `{ version, sessionId, heartbeatAt, open }`; US-008 adds `openedAt` and the ui.close rewrite.

userStories.title: Refresh throttle, lifecycle, store restore and marker file
userStories.description: As a user, I want the pane to be live without slowing the session down, and to survive reloads.
acceptanceCriteria: `$.ui.invalidate("ui.render")` is called through a throttle that allows at most 4 calls per second (trailing call kept); the reducer's `setModel` goes through it

The usage timer and the poller `start()` on `ui.open` (command or restore) and `stop()` on `ui.close` for every `e.origin` (`plugin`, `person`, `unload`); while closed only the `turn.*`/`tool.call` bookkeeping hooks do work
On `session.start` with `e.isInteractive === true`, if `$.store.get('pane')` is `{ open: true, view }`, the pane is reopened on that view after the binary check

The `ui.render` hook body is wrapped in try/catch: a throw renders `<Text color="red">cctop render error: <message></Text>` above the last successfully built tree (kept in the model); the registration also has `.catch`

Marker file: `writeMarker` writes `${$.env.HOME}/.cctop/pane/<sessionId>.json` = `{ "version": <plugin.json version>, "sessionId", "openedAt", "heartbeatAt", "open": true }` on open and on every poller tick, and rewrites it with `open: false` and a fresh `heartbeatAt` on `ui.close` (any origin); `$.fs` cannot delete so the file is never removed

Tests (`tests/pane/lifecycle.test.ts`) with the manual clock: 20 model changes in 1 s produce <= 4 invalidates plus one trailing; timers are cancelled after `ui.close`; store round-trip restores `view` on `session.start`; marker content after open, after a tick, after close; a throwing view renders the error line and the previous tree
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: cctop split fallback: Linux terminals and idempotency
userStories.description: As a user without function hooks on Linux, I want a new-window fallback and no duplicate dashboards.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/split.rs` adds `Host::LinuxWindow(String)` chosen on Linux (no multiplexer detected) in this order, first that resolves via a mockable `which`: `$TERMINAL`, `x-terminal-emulator`, `gnome-terminal`, `konsole`, `alacritty`, `kitty`, `xterm`; argv shapes: `<term> -e cctop run --session <id>` for `$TERMINAL`/`x-terminal-emulator`/`konsole`/`alacritty`/`xterm`, `gnome-terminal -- cctop run --session <id>`, and for kitty `kitten @ launch --type=os-window cctop run --session <id>` when `$KITTY_LISTEN_ON` is set else `kitty -e cctop run --session <id>`

`docs/hosts.md` has a row per Linux terminal (detection, command issued, `Verified: pending`) and the idempotency rule
